title: Lrp5 controls bone formation by inhibiting serotonin synthesis in the duodenum
authors: Yadav VK, Ryu JH, Suda N, Tanaka KF, Gingrich JA, Schütz G, et al.
population: Mice with global, gut-specific or osteoblast-specific Lrp5 and Tph1 mutations; samples from patients with LRP5 mutations
funder: This work was supported by grants from the March of Dimes foundation and the National Institutes of Health (to G.K.).
result: Lrp5 inhibited Tph1 expression in duodenal enterochromaffin cells; lowering blood serotonin normalised bone formation in Lrp5-deficient mice, and gut-specific Tph1 inactivation increased bone mass and prevented ovariectomy-induced bone loss; serotonin inhibited osteoblast proliferation through Htr1b and CREB. The authors state that gut-derived serotonin accounts for 95% of total serotonin, is taken up by platelets, and does not cross the blood-brain barrier. Animal data; later disputed by Cui and colleagues (2011).
